es: Detectar afirmaciones sin fuente en un mensaje, reescribirlas con atribución y cautela, y justificar cada cambio.

teaching.en: The post says that the school will close, but without a named source it is only a rumour, and hearsay is not proof.
teaching.es: El mensaje dice que el colegio cerrará, pero sin una fuente con nombre es solo un rumor, y un «me lo han contado» no es una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Un rumour circula sin respaldo; proof es incontable: no lleva plural.

teaching.en: Before you share the message, verify the claim with a reliable source, because a baseless story can spread in a few hours.
teaching.es: Antes de compartir el mensaje, verifica la afirmación con una fuente fiable, porque una historia infundada puede propagarse en pocas horas.
teaching.explanationEs: Verify = comprobar con una fuente; baseless = sin fundamento.
segments: Before you share the message, verify the claim with a reliable
source, because a baseless story can spread in a few hours.

teaching.en: «Obviously, the new rule is unfair» is a sweeping claim: the word obviously asks the reader to accept an opinion without proof.
teaching.es: «Obviously, the new rule is unfair» es una afirmación generalizada: la palabra obviously pide al lector que acepte una opinión sin pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Obviously, everyone knows o clearly presentan una opinión como si fuera un hecho.
segments: «Obviously, the new rule is unfair» is a sweeping claim: the
word obviously asks the reader to accept an opinion without proof.

teaching.en: Apparently, the school will close in June, but there is no proof yet, so a careful writer would hedge the claim with may or might.
teaching.es: Al parecer, el colegio cerrará en junio, pero todavía no hay pruebas, así que un redactor cuidadoso matizaría la afirmación con may o might.
teaching.explanationEs: Apparently marca que el dato viene de oídas; hedge = matizar con may, might, apparently.

teaching.en: These numbers suggest that the school may lose pupils next year, which is a cautious way to draw a conclusion from incomplete data.
teaching.es: Estas cifras apuntan a que el colegio podría perder alumnos el año próximo, una forma cauta de sacar una conclusión de datos incompletos.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest that + may expresa una inferencia probable, no una certeza.

teaching.en: An unverified message is not a fact until a source confirms it, and if the source was wrong, a responsible writer will retract the claim and debunk the rumour.
teaching.es: Un mensaje sin verificar no es un hecho hasta que una fuente lo confirma, y si la fuente se equivocó, un redactor responsable retirará la afirmación y desmontará el rumor.
teaching.explanationEs: Unverified = sin verificar; retract retira lo dicho y debunk demuestra que algo es falso.

prompt.es: Elige la reescritura más cauta de la primera afirmación del mensaje.

choices.text: The school will close in June, because the numbers are really terrible.
Obviously, the school may close in June, as everybody already knows.
Apparently, the school may close, but there is no proof yet.

feedback.es: Sustituye la certeza por apparently y may, y reconoce que faltan pruebas; las otras frases mantienen obviously o afirman el cierre sin matices.

hint.es: Busca la frase que baja la certeza y admite que faltan pruebas.

origin.text: Message: Obviously the school will close in June, because everyone knows that the numbers are terrible. A friend told me that the director has signed the papers.

prompt.es: Completa: «No hay fuente, así que debemos verificar la afirmación antes de compartirla.»

feedback.es: Verify significa comprobar con una fuente fiable: es el primer paso antes de difundir un mensaje.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa comprobar que algo es cierto.

origin.text: The post names no source, so we should ___ the claim before we share it with the whole group.

answer.text: An unverified message is not a fact until a source confirms it

feedback.es: Until a source confirms it marca la condición: sin fuente, el mensaje sigue siendo un rumor.

hint.es: La condición con until va al final de la frase.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del mensaje con el problema o la virtud que muestra.

pairs: A teacher told my cousin that it is true.
Everyone knows that the school will close.
Some experts say that the plan may help, but no study proves it.

feedback.es: Cada frase revela algo distinto: una opinión disfrazada, un dato de oídas, una afirmación sin fuente o una inferencia cautelosa.

prompt.es: Escucha a la verificadora y elige por qué matiza la afirmación en lugar de negarla.

choices.text: Because the council has taken no decision yet.
Because the council confirmed a real cut in the opening hours.
Because she wants the original poster to keep the rumour alive.

feedback.es: El ayuntamiento no ha decidido nada: no hay prueba del cierre, pero tampoco una negativa definitiva, así que lo prudente es matizar.

origin.audio: A fact-checker explains how she handled a viral message that said the town library would close. She contacted the council, which replied that no decision had been taken. She then wrote a correction: apparently, the library may reduce its hours, but there is no proof of a closure. She also asked the original poster to retract the claim.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema principal tiene esta afirmación de un mensaje viral?

choices.text: It is so cautious that it is useless to most readers.
It is a sweeping claim without any source or limit.
It names a source that nobody is able to check at all.

feedback.es: «Everybody», «every pupil» y «will harm» forman una afirmación enorme sin fuente ni matices.

origin.text: Viral message: Everybody knows that the new rule will harm the results of every pupil in the country.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje reenviado. ¿Qué actitud tiene la vecina hacia su información?

choices.text: She doubts it, because nobody at the depot has mentioned it.
She is certain because the council has already confirmed it.
She is convinced, although she admits there is no official confirmation.

feedback.es: Dice que nadie lo ha confirmado oficialmente y aun así está segura: convicción sin respaldo oficial, que el mensaje presenta como «apparently».

origin.text: Forwarded message: Apparently the council will cut the night bus from March. My neighbour, who works at the depot, says that nobody has officially confirmed it, but she is sure that it will happen.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige para qué pide la editora una nota con cada cambio.

choices.text: To make the correction clear to readers.
To protect the reporter from being blamed.
To make the article shorter before it is printed.

feedback.es: La nota explica qué se corrigió y por qué: el objetivo es que los lectores vean la corrección, no proteger a la reportera ni acortar el texto.

origin.audio: At the staff meeting, the editor reads a draft that says obviously the hospital will be closed next year. She stops and asks where the claim comes from. The reporter admits that it came from a message on social media. The editor tells her to verify it with the health board and, until then, to write that the closure is only a rumour. She also asks the reporter to explain each change in a short note, so that readers can see what was corrected and why.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué debe escribir la reportera mientras no se verifique el dato.

choices.text: That the hospital will close next year.
That the closure is only an unverified rumour.
That the health board has denied the closure.

feedback.es: Hasta comprobarlo con la autoridad sanitaria, el cierre debe presentarse como un rumor sin verificar, no como un hecho ni como un desmentido.

prompt.es: Marca tres afirmaciones dudosas, reescríbelas con fuente y cautela y justifica.

answer.text: I found three doubtful claims in the post. First, the school will close in June is presented as a fact, but no source is named, so it is only a rumour. I would rewrite it as: apparently, the school may close in June, but there is no proof yet. Second, the director has already signed the papers comes from a teacher who told someone's cousin, which is hearsay, so I would write that, according to an unverified account, the director may have signed them. Third, the new rule is clearly unfair is a sweeping claim that uses an opinion word, and I would change it to: some parents suggest that the rule may be unfair. I made these changes because every claim needs a source, and because cautious words such as apparently and may show what we do not know yet. Before sharing the post, we should verify it with the school.
accepted: I found three doubtful claims in the post. First, the school will close in June is presented as a fact, but no source is named, so it is only a rumour. I would rewrite it as: apparently, the school may close in June, but there is no proof yet. Second, the director has already signed the papers comes from a teacher who told someone's cousin, which is hearsay, so I would write that, according to an unverified account, the director may have signed them. Third, the new rule is clearly unfair is a sweeping claim that uses an opinion word, and I would change it to: some parents suggest that the rule may be unfair. I made these changes because every claim needs a source, and because cautious words such as apparently and may show what we do not know yet. Before sharing the post, we should verify it with the school.

The post contains three claims that I would not repeat. The claim about the closure is only a rumour, because nobody names a source, so I would say that, apparently, the school may close, although there is no proof. The claim about the signed papers is second-hand, so I would write that, according to a teacher, the director has signed them, and I would add that this is unverified. The claim that the new rule is unfair is an opinion presented as a fact, so I would turn it into: some parents say that it may be unfair. I changed these sentences because a reader must know who says what and how certain it is. Before we share anything, we should verify the post with the school and with the director.

feedback.es: Un buen informe marca tres afirmaciones, las reescribe con atribución y cautela, y explica que cada cambio añade una fuente o baja la certeza.

origin.text: Post shared in the parents' group: Obviously the school will close in June, because everyone knows that the numbers are terrible. A teacher told my cousin that the director has already signed the papers. The new rule on homework is clearly unfair and will harm the results of every pupil. Share this now, before it disappears!

prompt.es: Lee la respuesta de la editora al lector. ¿Qué actitud transmite?

choices.text: She defends the first version and refuses to change a single word.
She blames the reader for spreading an unverified message again.
She accepts the criticism and corrects the text carefully.

feedback.es: Reconoce el error («we should have verified») y reescribe con apparently y may: acepta la crítica y corrige el texto.

origin.text: Editor's reply: You are right that our first version said obviously the pool would close. We have now changed it to: apparently the pool may close, but there is no proof yet. We should have verified the claim before publishing it.
